Cc: procurement@greenarc.com
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form questions — invoice routing & VAT handling

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the draft order form. Procurement had a quick read and we have a few open items before we can route to Finance for approval: 

- Which legal entity will receive invoices (GreenArc has multiple payer entities; we need a clear recipient to generate PO and payment).
- Our tax team needs confirmation on how Redwood will handle VAT/withholding if services are rendered to our EU entity but invoiced in the US.
- Net terms request: our standard is Net 60 — they asked whether Net 45 is possible (they can escalate if needed).
- Minimum commitment: we prefer a single-year firm commitment rather than a stepped schedule; curious if you can offer a small true-up at year-end instead.

Can you confirm the invoice path and provide any tax residency evidence or precedent? I attached a short vendor onboarding checklist from our side (see attachment stub).

Thanks,
Ana Lopez
Senior Procurement Lead
GreenArc Systems

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form questions — invoice routing & VAT handling

Hi Ana — thanks for the clarity and the checklist. Short answers up front, then next steps: 

1) Invoice recipient: We can invoice the US entity by default (Redwood, Inc.). If GreenArc requires EU invoicing, we can route to Redwood Europe Sarl but that requires confirming the billing entity on the order form and may affect pricing (currency / VAT).

2) VAT / withholding: We typically do not gross-up for withholding unless contractually agreed. We can add a tax residency certification appendix and commit to provide evidence (tax residency certificate / W-8/W-9 as appropriate).

3) Net terms: We can accommodate Net 45 for first-year clients on a committed-tier. Net 60 is outside our standard without credit approval.

4) Minimum commit: Open to either a single firm-year commit or a stair-step. If you prefer a firm year with a year-end true-up, we can propose that as an option — it affects unit price bands.

Next steps I'd propose:
- Internal quick sync: kimberly (pricing) and ben (finance ops) to confirm the pricing impact of the firm-year vs staircase option.
- Legal redlines: loop in Karthik (commercial counsel) to prepare the order form redlines that capture invoice recipient, tax appendix, and net terms.
- I'll send a mutual action plan with dates so procurement and finance know what to expect.

Kimberly / Ben — can you weigh in on price delta for the two commit options? Karthik — can you take a first pass on the tax/invoice language after that?

Thanks,
Priyom
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priom_das@redwood.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Order form questions — invoice routing & VAT handling

Priyom / Ben — quick pricing note for the customer: 

- Firm 12-month commit (single-entity): ~5% premium to the baseline list for the guarantee.
- Stair-step (25/25/50 by quarter): no premium but pricing bands kick in later; customer may overcommit to hit lower bands.

Recommendation: Offer the firm-year with a calendar-year true-up clause (customer pays any shortfall at year-end at mid-band price). That gives GreenArc predictability and avoids later disputes.

On the legal side, we need explicit fields in the order form for:
- Invoice recipient entity and remit address; not just a billing contact.
- Tax residency appendix: what evidence we will accept and a timeline for delivery (we usually request within 10 business days of execution).
- Payment contact and PO number field to avoid routing delays.

I've attached my marked version of the order form with commercial edits — mainly the invoice entity table and a sample true-up schedule.

Thanks,
Kimberly
Director, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 15:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form questions — invoice routing & VAT handling (legal redlines)

Team / Ana — 

I reviewed Kimberly's commercial edits and drafted the legal changes. High-level summary of what I propose to include in the order form / MSA appendices: 

1) Invoice recipient: Add explicit "Invoice Recipient" table (entity name, tax ID, remit address, preferred currency). Redwood will invoice the entity specified on the table; any change to invoice recipient requires 30 days' notice.

2) Net terms: Convert the payment term to Net 45 as a commercial concession on this deal. Add a provision that late fees (1.5% monthly) apply after the grace period and that persistent Net 60 requests require credit review.

3) Taxes / Withholding: Add a Tax Appendix: (a) Customer is responsible for any withholding taxes unless a prior written agreement is in place; (b) Redwood will provide tax residency certificates (W-9 / W-8BEN-E) within 10 business days of request; (c) If withholding reduces amounts payable, parties will discuss a gross-up or offset; default is no gross-up.

4) True-up / Minimum commit: Incorporate Kimberly's year-end true-up language: compute committed units vs consumed units; any shortfall billed at the mid-band rate within 30 days after year-close.

5) Approval / Signature flow: Recommend DocuSign for the order form only (MSA already executed). Include a DocuSign envelope link in the final send.

I've attached a short FAQ on tax residency and a redlined order form. If GreenArc provides an EU invoice requirement, we should confirm whether pricing needs to be adjusted for VAT and currency exposure.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
